[{"id": "Unq4uwbiJJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🫂Ministries Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "OT-bYLlBeJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Ministries module holds the life of the church week by week. A Function is any service, meeting or event on the church calendar, from Sunday worship to a youth retreat. With functions you plan the order of service, take sign-ups, schedule the people who serve, check children in safely and record who came. The module also keeps your ministries, your song library and your counseling cases.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JZ7Z4yg0Nj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church Managers add and change functions, ministries, songs and settings. Church Staff can read them, and can add sign-ups, serving assignments and blocked dates, but change only the ones they made. Church People Editor users approve sign-ups, Church Finance users record payments, Church Pastoral Care users keep counseling cases, and Church Check-In volunteers run the Check-In Station. Members sign up, see when they serve and check in from the member portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nno5-lg6vE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To turn off the whole module, untick Ministries in Church Features. This also removes the Calendar, Register, Ministries, sign-up, attendance and serving pages from the website and the member portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "epdT06Yll5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Ministries workspace starts with the work that waits for you: Pending Team Responses (serving requests with no answer yet), Waitlisted Sign-Ups (sign-ups that wait for a free seat), Coming Up This Week, Church Calendar (it opens in a new tab) and the Check-In Station.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "E8vQm8fPOE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Under them, cards count the ministries and the songs, and a chart shows the weekly attendance of the last three months. The sidebar lists Functions, Coming Up This Week, Ministries, Check-In Station, Songs and Counseling Cases. The folders hold Function Planning (sign-ups and their reports), Attendance, Ministry Teams, Reports and Setup.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7FTEzM7bfm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "⛪Ministries", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fuH8ZHGx42", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Ministry is an area of the church's work, such as Youth, Worship or Hospitality. Functions, serving positions and expenses can belong to a ministry, so you see each ministry's events, team and spending in one place.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9IZ0R7wxFn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Name, Group and Team Coordinator are at the top of the Details tab. Two ministries of one church cannot have the same name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lIqrR7qX2y", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Status is Active or Inactive. A bulletin with the Ministries section prints the mission statement of each active ministry.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pu7cVk4GLM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Website section holds Publish, Mission Statement and Description. The Ministries page of the website shows each published, active ministry with its description and mission statement.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pqZQoWlWqq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Total Expenses adds up the submitted expenses that name the ministry. Only Church Managers and the finance team see it. The Ministries report, which check-in volunteers can open, shows no money.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rB9TZjAbWJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Recurring Functions lists the functions that repeat for this ministry. Click Create Recurring Function to start one (see Recurring Functions).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zQeCCERtlW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Connections tab lists the ministry's functions, its team positions and its expenses.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "V5Vnsc2Tjc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🗓️Functions", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jBXKi2DWz0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Function is one service, meeting or event: Sunday Worship on November 15, the Tuesday Bible study, the church picnic. Everything about the event hangs on it: the order of service, the people who serve, the sign-ups, the room bookings, the bulletin, the collection and the attendance.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YctvghHJF2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: For Sunday Worship, the office adds a Function for Sunday at 10:00. On the Service Plan tab, the worship leader lists the songs and the sermon. The ministry team schedule asks three greeters and a sound technician to serve. On Sunday, volunteers check the children in at the Check-In Station, and the counters enter the offering in a Collection for this Function. On Monday, the Attendance Total shows who came.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qGuJqCtbqV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add a function", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2Ma_W7CgET", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Functions and click Add Function.
2. Type the name, choose the Type (such as Sunday Morning Service or Group Meeting) and the Associated Ministry, and set the Start Date, Start Time and End Time. Add the address if it is not at the church.
3. To show it on the public website, tick Publish in the Website and Streaming section.
4. Save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "H14G7diCX-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit refuses an end before the start, an Online Meeting Link that does not start with https:// or that has a space, sign-ups that close before they open, a Repeat Until before the Start Date, a Minimum Age above the Maximum Age, and a Minimum Grade above the Maximum Grade.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "b6m3o8GWCk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The form has five tabs:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "F4dvkFF9eT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Details: what, when and where, the Website and Streaming settings, the Recurrence and the Associations (other records that the function is about).
- Service Plan: the Schedule (the order of service) and the Team Needs (the people who must serve).
- Registration: the sign-up settings (see Function Sign-Ups).
- Attendance: the attendance total, the headcount, the attendance rows and Who Can Check In.
- Connections: the sign-ups, check-ins, team assignments, room bookings, bulletins, meeting minutes and collections of the function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "n0mhgmRKah", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Under Actions on a saved function are Check-In Station, Book a Room, New Bulletin, Email the Team and Fill Open Needs. Under View are the Team Schedule, Signed-Up Items and Signed-Up People reports. Each one shows only to the users who may use it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "20LEwysR2w", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Function types and templates", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DwtRYBMZi_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit starts with function types such as Sunday Morning Service, Prayer Meeting, Communion, Baptism and Group Meeting. You can add more under Function Types in the Setup folder.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hALOBIw5EJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A function type can name a Template Function: an earlier function whose details you want to copy. On a new function of that type, set the Start Date first, then click Fill From Template. Churchit copies most details, the schedule (moved to the new date, at the same times) and the attendance rows.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NP0mWctGkT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Plan the service", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2RHgbdrXz0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Plan the order of a service in the Schedule table on the Service Plan tab. Each row has a Start time. Tick Header on a row to make it a heading for a part of the service, such as Worship or Response. The bulletin prints the schedule as its Order of Worship.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "g3ncNiSbuq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A row can link a Song, a Sermon, a Person or another record. For a song, choose the Arrangement and the Key. Leave the Key empty to use the key of the arrangement, or the song's default key. A row whose Arrangement is not one of the song's arrangements cannot be saved.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JZ5vb6jnji", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Displayed (ticked at first) and Printed record how the words of a song were copied. Tick Streamed or Recorded on the function when the service went out live or was recorded. The Song Usage report counts these uses for your CCLI report.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GFtU71mi4c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Team Notes are for the people who serve only. They see them on the Serving page of the member portal. The bulletin never prints them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A9wb3DUyV8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On the website", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8C-91VWPVt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Publish shows the function on the public Calendar page and in the calendar feed. A function over several days shows on each day. Visitors click it to see the time, the address with an Open map link, the rooms of its approved bookings, and the links below.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bLHWmPb55O", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Link Only keeps a published function off the Calendar page, the feed, the home page and the Register list. Share its link instead, such as /calendar?event=FUNC-0042, or a Register link with ?function=FUNC-0042. Function IDs are numbers in order, so a person can guess the link: do not use Link Only to keep a private event secret.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9pOsrFNzrR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Online Meeting Link: an https link to join online, such as a video call. The Calendar shows Join online, and the link is in the calendar feed, on the Serving page and in a sign-up's calendar file.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ElFo1IldTF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Streamed: when your church has a Live Stream Link (see Watch Live in the Website manual), the Calendar shows Watch live on the function from 15 minutes before it starts until it ends.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "d-jsNyNsaW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- With more than one church, the Calendar of a church with published branch churches offers Include branch churches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QqWcwRAbtn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Attendance", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pTfAMavMwZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Record who came on the Attendance tab. Add a row for each person with an attendance type, or click Add Multiple under the table to add many people at once, for example from a sign-in sheet. Check-ins and sign-ups add their rows by themselves. A person can be on only one row.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7gtNf4bmdd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Attendance Total counts only the rows whose type is Confirmed, Assumed or Checked-In. Signed-Up and Absent rows do not count, and neither does a type that you add yourself under Attendance Types. A function counts its attendance only from its Start Date, so rows that you add ahead of time, for example from a roster, count once the day comes. Each day, Churchit updates the totals of the functions of the last week.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BaueV30yoq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Headcount is the number of people in the room, named or not (see Headcount under Check-In Station).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "z2o9vTXV8x", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Several people can change attendance at once: a check-in, a sign-up and a member's change in the portal each change only that person's row. A sign-up never replaces a row that says more, such as Checked-In or Absent. If someone checks a person in while you have the function open, your save stops and asks you to reload, so no row is lost.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WzKmpmyqJB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sign-in sheet. Print (Ctrl+P) on a function opens the Attendance Sign-In Sheet, with each person and their household, such as John & Jane Smith, and Yes under Visitor? for visitors. Guests of a confirmed sign-up who have no Person record get a row too.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "OMVqpn1EvU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Attendance in the member portal", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vlJ-h-fZd5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members see their own attendance on the Attendance page of the member portal. Attended lists the functions up to today that have them in the attendance, with the type. Coming up lists the functions after today that they signed up for, with the status of the sign-up.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zFPnlfJS-i", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To let members correct their own attendance, tick Members Can Change Their Attendance in Portal Settings. Each Attended row then offers I was there (saved as Confirmed) and I was not there (saved as Absent), and the total follows. A Checked-In row can be changed only in the desk.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tgUetrVKxU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Find functions and reports", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FR2wVCx3u4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Coming Up This Week shows the functions of the next days first. The Functions list shows the newest dates first, so a service today can be far down the list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "X2atU-TpDk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When a form asks for a Function, such as a Bulletin or a Collection, the list shows the functions from today on first, then the past ones.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LRkj57ZH1f", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Church Calendar opens the calendar of functions. A function with All Day ticked, or with no Start Time, shows in the all-day row, and one with no End Time shows as one hour long. Drag a function to move it to another day or time, or drag its lower edge to change the end. The schedule rows and the room bookings do not move with it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "q1bepn1Ln3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The attendance reports are in the Attendance folder: Church Attendance (the last four weeks at first), Check-Ins by Function, Attendance by Person (the last three months at first) and Function Count by Type. The first three have a Group filter to see only the meetings of one group.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CBGpzzliJR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Function Planning folder holds the sign-up reports, the Recurring Functions report and the Functions Report.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "19W5TyUzOU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🔁Recurring Functions", "col": 12}}, {"id": "J7zHP-x7Uc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Most church events repeat: the Sunday service every week, the women's Bible study every other Tuesday, the elders' meeting on the first Monday of the month. Set up the function once, and Churchit makes each occurrence for you.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sUhnZbzXww", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The function that you set up is the template. A template is a rule, not an event: it does not show on the calendar, nobody checks in to it, and no report counts it. Churchit makes the occurrences from it, each one a normal Function that copies the template's schedule, team needs, associations, sign-up settings, discounts and attendance roster. Requested and Approved room bookings move to the new date too.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IGOV8ATUs1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: The youth group meets every Wednesday at 7 PM in the fellowship hall. You make one Function, Youth Group, with Automatically Recreate ticked, Weekly on Wednesday, and a room booking. Churchit makes the next eight Wednesdays at once, each with its own booking of the hall. Before Christmas, you add the Wednesday of Christmas week to Skip Dates, so there is no meeting that week.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "f4CsUU1k59", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Make a function repeat", "col": 12}}, {"id": "O8phMFVJ_g", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. On the Function, open the Recurrence section and tick Automatically Recreate.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xyQ4khd6-l", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Choose a Repeat Frequency: Daily, Weekly, Monthly or Yearly. In Repeat Every, type 1 for every time, or 2 for every second day, week, month or year.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "S91I3-LBnl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. For Weekly, choose the day in Repeat Day of Week.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KJvbwseNhU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. For Monthly, choose Repeat Monthly By. With Day of Month, type the day, such as the 15th (a day after the end of a short month moves to its last day). With Weekday, choose the week and the day, such as the Second Sunday or the Last Friday.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3JIcOdACMj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. If you want, set Repeat Until to stop on a date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2plYBl62rx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "6. Save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fbSxNPuzfE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "You can also open a Ministry and click Create Recurring Function to start one that belongs to that ministry.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dXttmwLnIF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How occurrences are made", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VJrQRRHJhx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Churchit makes the first occurrences a moment after you save the template. Each day, it makes the next ones ahead of time, for the number of weeks in Create Weeks Ahead (8 at first), so they show on the calendar early.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZpChsCJJjj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The people in the template's Attendance table are a roster. Each occurrence copies them, except people who have died. They count as attendance only once that occurrence starts.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "suTLdhemkm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The sign-up open and close dates and the discount dates move with each occurrence's start date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1AxvQFx9rs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A change to the template reaches only the occurrences that Churchit makes after the change. To change occurrences that already exist, edit or delete them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "772gt2vtZu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Add a date to Skip Dates when the function does not happen on that day. When you delete an occurrence, its room bookings are deleted and its date is added to Skip Dates, so it is not made again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FDTEnfTTE4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- If a room is already booked at the new time, the occurrence is made without that booking, and a comment on it names the room and the time. A room that needs approval gets a Requested booking.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Z30-qg8ots", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Untick Automatically Recreate at any time to stop.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QpHv9VBV2B", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Group meetings", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2lidRUM_Ht", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Function can be a meeting of a Group, such as a small group or a class. Choose the group in the Group field of the function, not in Associations. The group must belong to the church of the function, and a function with a group cannot be shared with all churches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8qor34V91H", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To give a group a weekly or monthly meeting, open the group and click Actions, then Set Up Meetings. A new Function opens with the group, the type Group Meeting and Automatically Recreate ticked. Choose the day, the time and the address, and save. Record the attendance on each meeting, not on this schedule.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XTpVR__4Nu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Attendance reminder. The day after a group meeting with no attendance recorded, Churchit emails the group's leaders a link to record it in the member portal. It sends nothing when the site has no outgoing email account.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ev3y0ewKhr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Did Not Meet. When a group did not meet, tick Did Not Meet on the Attendance tab of that meeting. Churchit then sends the leaders no reminder, and the Group Attendance report does not count it. A leader can also do this in the member portal (see Lead a Group in the People manual). Attendance Recorded On shows when a leader last saved the attendance.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "o42_REzOXn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📝Function Sign-Ups", "col": 12}}, {"id": "s2ZzsdArjl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Function Sign-Up is a person's place at a function: who comes, what they bring, what they chose and what they owe. Use sign-ups when you need to know ahead of time who comes, such as for a dinner, a retreat, a class or a mission trip. Members sign up in the member portal, guests on the website's Register page, and staff in the desk.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gHzpZo5Yb6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: The women's retreat takes 40 people, costs $75, and needs 10 people to bring a dish. On the Function, you tick Allow Sign-Ups and Allow Guest Sign-Ups, set Capacity to 40, add a Selection called Adult with the price $75, and add a Sign-Up Item called Dish with Quantity Needed 10. Anna signs up on the Register page with her sister and one dish. She pays online, and the sign-up is Confirmed. When the 40 places are taken, new sign-ups go on the waitlist.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eCNNF9PUg6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open a function for sign-ups", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gv5mcbA1YG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On the Registration tab of the Function:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LcJC_YHFzN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Tick Allow Sign-Ups. Signed-in members can then sign up.
2. To let guests sign up on the website too, tick Allow Guest Sign-Ups, and tick Publish on the Details tab.
3. Set the limits and prices that you need (see below), then save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Y0c2Bre279", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sign-Ups Open On and Sign-Ups Close On set when members and guests can sign up. Leave a date blank for no limit. When Sign-Ups Close On is blank, members cannot sign up for a function that started before today. Staff can add a sign-up in the desk at any time.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "j9VVvfY4n7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Where people sign up", "col": 12}}, {"id": "s27CC8DepR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Register page: a person who is not signed in signs up on the Register page of the website. It shows the published functions that take guests and start today or later. The page is not in the website menu: put a link to /register on a web page, in an email or in a QR code, or add it to the menu (see the Website manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TMTchr4Uz4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A guest types a name and an email, and can add a phone number and notes. A guest never sees the name of anyone else.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iuyxOJCtxl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The member portal: a signed-in member sees every function of their church that takes sign-ups now, also one that is not published or does not take guests, on the Sign-Ups page. A function with selections or questions sends the member to the Register page, where they choose the options and answer the questions. The member signs up as their own person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5O9_fxISbk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The desk: staff add a Function Sign-Up for a person. Only functions with Allow Sign-Ups ticked are offered.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PE4BLiebAd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Bringing others. On the Register page, a signed-in member can tick the people of their own household who come too, and anyone can click Add a person and type the name of someone else who comes. Each person takes a place. A registration can bring at most 20 other people.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ffFXvfyNLf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Guests and their Person. A guest's sign-up has no Person at first. A moment later, Churchit links it to the one person whose name and email or phone match. If nobody matches, Churchit adds the guest as a Visitor with the Source Sign-Up, and records possible duplicates for staff to check (see Clean Data in the People manual). If the matched person already has a sign-up for the function, the new sign-up stays without a Person, with a comment that names the other sign-up.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NRoGtTJuOW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who comes and what they bring", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dG2dMAy8uA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Each person can have only one sign-up for a function. A Cancelled sign-up does not count.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4Ez-RGV7Z8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Attending says whether the person who signs up comes. While it is ticked, that person is in the Attendees table, with the other people who come.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ebAwu6s9N7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- While a sign-up is Confirmed, each attendee is on the function's attendance with the type Signed-Up. When the sign-up stops being Confirmed, Churchit removes that row only while it still says Signed-Up.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FDNJFib_Ne", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Sign-Up Items are things or jobs that the function needs, such as food or setting up chairs. Add them to the function's Sign-Up Items table with the Quantity Needed. People choose items and quantities on their sign-up, and Quantity Signed Up on the function adds them up. Tick Limited on an item to refuse sign-ups when its quantity is reached. A sign-up that only brings items, with Attending unticked, takes no place. Make the list of items under Sign-Up Items in the Setup folder.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vESY_U4meE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Status", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jvMYYWjLKt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each sign-up has a status that only Churchit sets:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "m2mwq8t6XT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Confirmed: the person has a place.
- Pending: the sign-up waits for approval or for payment, and holds its places meanwhile.
- Waitlisted: the function is full, and the sign-up waits for a free place.
- Cancelled: the sign-up no longer counts. It keeps its record, and the person can sign up again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xsby3F8IJ2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To cancel a sign-up, open it, click the ... menu, then Cancel Registration. A member cancels their own sign-up on the Sign-Ups page of the member portal with Cancel my sign-up. A member can open a sign-up that staff added for them, but only the church office can change or cancel it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QnmqE3GDuf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Capacity and the waitlist", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QdXiITjVpG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Capacity is the number of people who can come. Leave it at 0 for no limit. Add Selections when people choose an option, such as Adult or Child, each with its own price and capacity if needed. Each attendee then chooses one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "857CFt3yvP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When a capacity is full, a new sign-up is Waitlisted, and the whole party waits together. A sign-up that staff move to another function counts as new there: if that function is full, it is Waitlisted, and its places in the first function go to that function's waitlist.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QXFlzIXSFx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A party larger than a capacity cannot sign up. When places become free, Churchit gives them to the oldest waiting party that fits. Places become free when a sign-up is cancelled, declined or deleted, when a party removes an attendee, when a payment hold ends, or when you raise a capacity.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "R-baDm84vX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: The dinner has 50 places, and all are taken. The Jones family of four signs up and is Waitlisted. Then a couple cancels: two places are free, but the Jones family needs four, so they keep waiting. Mr. Brown, who signed up alone after them, gets one of the places. Later a family of three cancels. Now four places are free, so the Jones family is Confirmed and gets an email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tRX0kwtnqF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Approval", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Y8SkYi_Mhm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tick Sign-Ups Need Approval to approve each sign-up yourself. A new sign-up is then Pending and holds its places until you decide. Open it and click Actions, then Approve or Decline. Only Church Manager and Church People Editor users can do this. A declined sign-up is Cancelled, and its places go to the waitlist. When an approved sign-up adds people or items, it waits for approval again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YezwjekIAg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Prices and discounts", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tJF4w95eaL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Give each Selection a price for each attendee, and each Sign-Up Item a price for each one. Churchit works out the Amount Due of a sign-up: the price of each attendee's selection, plus each item's price times its quantity, less the discount. The person who signs up cannot change a price.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QRow4bGz3L", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add rows to Discounts on the Registration tab:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tpk7SWZNuM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Code: applies when the person types its code in Discount Code on the Register page. Capital letters do not matter. The box shows only while the function has a valid code.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VjUJm_BLD_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Early Bird: applies to sign-ups made on or before its Valid Until date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "odR-a5mAuO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Group: applies when a sign-up brings at least its Minimum Attendees. Use it only when the selections have a price.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Y9FGMPze4x", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Freely Given: applies to every sign-up.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "53cM3DMFAU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each discount takes its Amount off, or its Percent when Amount is empty. A Valid Until date ends any discount after that day. When more than one discount applies, only the largest comes off. The amount due is never below 0.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tqGHf2qR0u", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Freely given. \"Freely you have received; freely give\" (Matthew 10:8). When a function has a price, its form asks you to consider giving it freely. Click Offer It Freely to add a Freely Given discount of 100 percent. Every sign-up is then free, sign-ups that wait for payment are confirmed, and the Register page shows each price as freely given. A freely given function needs no Sign-Up Fund, unless the discount has a Valid Until date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Uq7RCLbY5m", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Payments", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ySnBb1MwAi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When a function has a price and is not freely given, choose a Sign-Up Fund on the Registration tab. The fund must belong to the church of the function, or be shared.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Z1Pv8J48WN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- With online giving (a payment gateway in Giving Settings): a sign-up with an amount due is Pending and holds its places for 24 hours. The person gets an email with a Pay now link, and the Register page shows the link too. When the payment arrives, Churchit records it in a collection for the fund and confirms the sign-up.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gulJNS4Yhc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The collection row has no person, so the payment is not on a giving statement. If the sign-up is not paid in 24 hours, Churchit cancels it and gives its places to the waitlist.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8SfavttWJo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Without online giving: a sign-up with an amount due is Confirmed at once, with the payment status Unpaid. The Register page and the confirmation email ask the person to pay at the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XcmLtRRiEv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When a person pays in cash or by check, open the sign-up and click Actions, then Record Offline Payment, and put the money in the weekly collection. If a payment arrives after the hold ended, or a paid sign-up is cancelled or declined, the payment status becomes Refund Due and Church Finance gets an alert.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VInCxx0uax", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Refund the payment at the payment processor, then click Actions, then Record Refund (see the Finances manual). Only Church Finance and Church Manager users record payments and refunds, and only a Church Manager can delete a paid sign-up. A paid sign-up cannot add anything that costs more, or move to another function: make a new sign-up instead.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JPfKrwi2gI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Questions", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1VAROhHgBJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To ask questions when people register, such as a T-shirt size or allergies, make a Question Set (see Question Sets) and choose it in Question Set on the Registration tab. The Register page asks the questions for the person who signs up and for each person they bring.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QPqTXUE-Es", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A required question must be answered for each person. You see the answers in the Answers section of each sign-up and in the Function Registrations report. Staff cannot type answers in the desk, so to add a sign-up for a function with required questions, use the Register page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dHBoRJKQq6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Emails and reminders", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sYLWZQIJzW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Confirmation: each time a sign-up becomes Confirmed (when it is approved, paid, moved off the waitlist or moved to another function), Churchit emails the person who signed up a confirmation with a calendar file. Pending and Waitlisted sign-ups get none. To change the text, edit the Email Template Sign-Up Confirmation. To stop it, delete that template.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CLBAFdsr3B", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Payment: the Email Template Sign-Up Payment Due holds the text of the email with the Pay now link.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tGMt9JNErF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Reminder: set Reminder Days on the Registration tab to the number of days before the function. 0 sends none. The person who signed up for each Confirmed sign-up gets one reminder by email, and one text if they agreed to texts for Event Registrations. The other attendees get no reminder. Edit the Email Template Sign-Up Reminder to change its words.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B1dLTeuLsu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The emails have a See your sign-up link for a person with a portal login. Churchit sends them only when the site has an outgoing email account. A person who said no to Event Registrations gets no reminder.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "e2nEEVu21r", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Reports", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GbALVjgukR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Function Registrations report shows one row for each person who comes, with the sign-up, their selection, the status and the payment. Choose a function to see a column for each of its questions, with each person's answer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "oWh6XmrMon", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Function Sign-Up Items report shows who brings what.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ztLLLzO7CU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With more than one church, a sign-up belongs to the church of its function. The sign-ups of a shared function are shared too.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "D6vOe2sBOs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📋Question Sets", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p_Ax5LGUl7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Question Set is a list of questions that your church asks people: on a sign-up, on a room booking, or as a form of its own on the website. The answers stay on the record that the person filled in.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xft93wi6L-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: For the children's camp, you make a Question Set with Child's T-shirt size (a choice of S, M, L), Allergies (a paragraph) and \"I agree to the camp rules\" (a required tick). You choose it on the camp's Function. Each parent who registers answers the questions for each child, and the Function Registrations report shows every answer in one table.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IBvZTQVFk6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Make a question set", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BUc_J9sjSq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open Question Sets (in the Forms folder of the Settings sidebar), click Add Question Set and give it a Title. Then add one row for each question:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p_QcfgkcEy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Question: the question as people read it, such as T-shirt size.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DU0GWANVtd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Answer Type: a line of text (Data), a paragraph (Small Text), a choice from a list (Select), a tick (Check), a date, a whole number (Int), an email address or a phone number.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kdfpWGovuI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Required: tick it when people must answer. A required tick must be ticked, for example to agree to the rules.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r_OBBQd5Uz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Choices: for a Select question, type each choice on a new line.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DkK910i4hH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each question gets an Answer Name, made from the question. Two questions in one set cannot have the same Answer Name. Do not change an Answer Name after people answer, because their answers are kept under it. A question cannot depend on the answer to another question: to ask different people different questions, make a second set.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w1GpTdibWw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each answer keeps the question as it was asked, so a later change to the set does not change old answers. With more than one church, a Question Set belongs to one church. Tick Shared with All Churches to let every church use it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Vu26UQihhb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Describe the Form with AI. When AI is turned on (see the Foundations manual), a new Question Set has the button Describe the Form. Type what the form should ask, for example \"A camp form: child name, age, T-shirt size, and a tick to agree to the rules\", and click Draft.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XN4xdSgMMw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Click Open Draft to open the Question Set filled in and not saved. Check each question and save. When a question needs something that no Answer Type can do, such as a file, the AI says that the form cannot be drafted.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0sGOn0yIW4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Forms on the website", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eyLAksz6E_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To use a Question Set as a form on its own, tick Publish as a Form in the Website Form section and save. Anyone can then answer it at /form/new?question_set= followed by the name of the set, such as QSET-0001.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-N10podUtX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Click Open Form under Links on the Question Set to open it, and copy its address into a web page, an email or a QR code. The form asks for a first name, a last name and an email address, then the questions. Tick Members Only to let only signed-in members answer: their answer is then linked to their own Person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "G5NTkBji1D", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each answer is a Form Response, in the Forms folder of the Settings sidebar and on the Connections tab of its Question Set. After a guest sends a form, Churchit finds the person with the same name and email, or adds them as a Visitor with the Source Form. The response then shows Processed. A response that stays New still needs its person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-95D3DV-DB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To follow up each answer, add the trigger Form Submitted to a Follow-up Workflow and choose the Question Set (see Follow-up in the People manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "e3Xe8-8CDw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Charge for a form. Before you charge, remember \"Freely you have received; freely give\" (Matthew 10:8): a form with no Price is free. To charge, give the Question Set a Price and a Fund. After a person sends the form, they go to the payment page. When the payment arrives, Churchit records it in a collection and the response shows Paid. After you refund a payment at the payment processor, open the Form Response and click Record Refund.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NdNIyXZTwK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With more than one church, a response belongs to the church of its Question Set. The responses to a shared Question Set are shared too, and the person's own church follows them up.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bU64qOs5sP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you anonymize a person, the answers on their own records are removed. On a sign-up, only their own answers are removed, and the answers of the other people stay.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "90QIG0b5I3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🙋Ministry Teams", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FK4dFpSulC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A ministry team is the people who serve in a ministry, such as greeters, ushers, nursery workers or the sound team. Churchit asks each person by email, or by text, whether they can serve at a function, keeps their answer, reminds them before the day, and helps you fill the gaps.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DE3wIhIC0p", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: The Hospitality ministry has a Greeter position with eight people. Sunday Worship needs two greeters. You click Fill Open Needs on the Function: Churchit asks the two people who served longest ago. Tom opens the link in the email and clicks Accept.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "OL22oPzTXo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sarah declines because she is away, so the team coordinator gets an email, and you click Fill Open Needs again to ask the next person. The ministry has Remind Days Before set to 3, so three days before Sunday, Tom and the new greeter get a reminder.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ftgXbZZgvm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Positions", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IQXsjTefJL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Ministry Team Position is one job on a ministry's team, such as Greeter in the Hospitality ministry.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nAGltnRUi_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Add the people who can fill the position under People. Only these people can be asked for it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ecapKUEvB-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Most Times a Month on each row limits how often a person is asked. 0 means no limit. Members set this number themselves on the Serving page of the member portal, under How often you serve.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UIdHqRa7H8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Tick Needs Background Check when the position needs a current, cleared Background Check, such as Nursery Worker. Under Required Checks, pick the kinds of checks it needs, for example Criminal Background and Child Safety Training. Leave it blank to accept any cleared check. Each one must be cleared and still current on the day of the function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DOGvuXnA5w", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Tick Block People Without Checks to refuse an assignment for someone without the checks. Without it, you only get a warning. Adding such a person to People also shows a warning.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JdqiKgmpd4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On the Ministry, set the Team Coordinator, who gets an email when someone declines, and Remind Days Before: how many days before a function the people serving get a reminder. 0 sends no reminder.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kz6PJq4wTG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Plan who must serve", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5szaZE667E", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On a Function, list the positions that it needs, and how many people each needs, in Team Needs on the Service Plan tab. Recurring functions and Fill From Template copy these needs. Notes on a need is a note to the people in that position: each person sees only the note of their own position.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LW0zDIi8Ai", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Ask people to serve", "col": 12}}, {"id": "re82rwrFXu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Fill Open Needs. Click Actions, then Fill Open Needs, on the Function. The Ministry Team Schedule and Ministry Team Grid reports have the same button: it fills every function in the dates, church and ministry of the filters.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ovo8OCroCs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- For each position, it takes people from the position's People, and asks first the person who served longest ago, or never.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2p6hdtIAF-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- It does not ask a person who is blocked on that date, who serves at the same time, who lacks a check that the position needs, who already has their Most Times a Month, or who has died. It asks a person for one position of a function only.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3AzOAHbAfw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- It never asks a person again for a place that they were already asked about, also when they declined. After someone declines, click it again to fill the place.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SRbFMuUGDS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- It does not fill a function that has started.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BNitwFrtLn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Ask one person. On the Connections tab of the Function, add a Ministry Team Assignment with the position and the person. Churchit warns you, but still saves, when the person has a blocked date then, serves at another function at the same time, lacks a needed background check, already has their Most Times a Month, or has no email address. The function, position and person cannot change after you save: delete the assignment and make a new one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XWjBJTgRqe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Requests, answers and reminders", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TsHMmG-eZb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each new assignment is Pending. Once a day, each person gets one email that lists their new requests. To send the waiting requests at once, click Send Requests Now on the Ministry Team Assignment list. Requested On stays empty until the request is sent, so the list shows which requests still wait.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UVz8oZlBEt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Each request has a link to Accept or Decline, with an optional reason. The link works without signing in. The person can also answer on the Serving page of the member portal, and on its home page. They can change their answer until the function starts.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_FA77WTkW_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Status of the assignment shows the answer: Pending, Accepted or Declined.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SYC3zHCoQe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When someone declines, the Team Coordinator gets an email, and the place is open again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Plh5xs95ru", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Each person who has not declined gets one reminder, once the function is Remind Days Before away. A request sent that same day counts as the reminder for that day, so a person asked late gets the reminder the next day.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ORRRo0V1jY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- If the site can send texts, each request and reminder also goes by text to the people who said yes to texts for Serving (see Consent in the Communications manual). The emails go to everyone asked to serve.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PZB1UYw_iC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "No email goes out until the site has an outgoing Email Account. A person with no email address and no text consent is never asked, so check the warning when you save. Change the words in the Email Templates Ministry Team Request, Ministry Team Reminder, Ministry Team Decline and Ministry Team Replacement.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UcBU-qH96f", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On the Serving page, Show the schedule opens the order of service of each function where the member serves. While they have not declined, it also shows the key and arrangement of each song, the team notes, the note for their position and the rehearsal media of the songs.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XvuAcwSo13", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Email the team. To write to everyone serving at a function, click Actions, then Email the Team, on the Function. It goes to each person asked who has not declined, in BCC. The email is kept on the function's timeline, and a message names anyone without an email address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "L9ryjCse4C", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When a volunteer cannot come", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hu2O2Ul26N", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A volunteer who cannot come can ask someone else to take their place. On the Serving page, or on the page that the request email opens, they click Ask someone else and choose a person. The list shows only the people of the position who are free then.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hLPf3MIzra", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The person they choose gets a request at once. The volunteer still serves until that person accepts. A volunteer can have only one such request waiting at a time.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3_oeao8iiY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When the person accepts, the volunteer's assignment changes to Declined with the reason Replaced by and the name, and the Team Coordinator gets an email that names who takes the place.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wy1DhJQqwZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When the person declines, nothing changes for the volunteer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gCEm2M1iaO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Either way, the volunteer gets an email with the answer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SqAtjCZqIS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: Sarah is on the nursery for Sunday but her son is sick. On the Serving page she clicks Ask someone else and chooses Mary. Mary accepts from her email. Sarah's assignment changes to Declined, Replaced by Mary, and the nursery coordinator gets an email that Mary takes the place.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "k8CUBFTiGB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Blocked dates", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mCkL5EYnR4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Ministry Team Block holds the dates when a person cannot serve, such as a vacation. Tick Whole Household to block everyone in their family. Members add and remove their own blocks on the Serving page. Blocks only warn: they do not stop an assignment, but Fill Open Needs skips the person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "aHeVvV5NiF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A block can repeat. Set Repeat to Weekly, Every Other Week or Monthly on the Same Weekday, and if you want, a Repeat Until date. Monthly uses the weekday and week of the From Date, for example the first Sunday. A repeating block must end before it repeats: a weekly block can be at most 7 days long. A monthly block that starts on a fifth Sunday covers only the months that have a fifth Sunday.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "T3zujc0J2b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: Tom works every other weekend. He adds a block on the Serving page from Saturday to Sunday, with Repeat Every Other Week. Fill Open Needs then never asks him on those weekends.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bBP5r7DNPN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With branch churches, only the person's own church can add a block for them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iY7xGVjUTf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Calendar link for volunteers", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sRksP-SGbZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members can see the functions where they serve in the calendar on their phone or computer. On the Serving page, they click Make a calendar link, then Subscribe, or copy the link into their calendar app. The calendar keeps itself up to date. Anyone with the link can see where the member serves, so Stop this link and make a new one replaces a link that was shared by mistake.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gy1dFYEc9F", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Team Schedule and Team Grid", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8xHdLFlPGC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Ministry Team Schedule report shows the positions of each function in a date range: how many people each needs, how many accepted or did not answer yet, how many places are open, and who was asked. Tick Only Open Positions to see the gaps. On a Function, View, then Team Schedule, opens it for that function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "R7kDf9o0bk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Ministry Team Grid report shows several weeks at once: a row for each position and a column for each function. Each cell shows the open places in red and the people asked: green for Accepted, orange for Pending and gray for Declined. Click an open place to ask someone for it. It shows 8 weeks at first, and at most 60 functions.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "y1ADNL-Y-F", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Last Served and Times Served (90 Days) on the Connections tab of the Person form count the functions where the person accepted an assignment. Filter the Person list on them to find people who have not served lately.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dfBjUfXlkj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "✅Function Check-Ins", "col": 12}}, {"id": "k-fuS62AKk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Function Check-In records that a person arrived at a function. Check-ins keep children safe: each child gets a name tag with a security code, the adult who brings them gets a matching pickup tag, and a volunteer releases the child only to someone with the right code. Check-ins also fill in the attendance of the function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZyEsxgZUwb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "There are four ways to check in:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8vbAooVx7I", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Check-In Station: a volunteer at the door finds families by name or phone and checks them in. This is the main way.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qaixNU-I3a", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The self check-in kiosk: families check themselves in on a tablet at the door.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5JzleQINbW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Pre check-in: a member chooses who comes in the member portal before they leave home, and shows a code at the door.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WNJkTjtilF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- By hand: staff add a Function Check-In in the desk, or tick people in the Person list and click Actions, then Check In. These give no security code, so use the station for children who need a pickup tag.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lWjydezlH2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: The church has ticked Print Security Codes in Check-In Settings. On Sunday at 9:45, the Smith family arrives at the children's wing. The volunteer types \"Smith\" at the Check-In Station, taps the two children and clicks Check In.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "L8iB6I9Unn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Two name tags print with the code K7M2, and a pickup tag with the same code prints for the father. After the service, the father shows his pickup tag. The volunteer clicks Verify Pickup, types K7M2, sees both children and the people allowed to collect them, and releases the children.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_XXMV2oYlU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each check-in has a Kind: Regular, Guest (a visitor added at the station) or Volunteer (a person who serves). A Volunteer check-in gets no security code, is not counted in the room capacity, and does not start a follow-up card for a first visit. Every kind sets the person's attendance row to Checked-In. A person can be checked in only once to a function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "E9qkcBd1Ro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Check-In Station", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fL1Q7TuYIy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Check-In Station is the quickest way to check people in as they arrive. Open it from the sidebar, or from Actions, then Check-In Station, on a Function. Church Check-In volunteers use it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Is5pwi3bN-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Choose the Function at the top. The station opens on the function last used on that computer when it is today, or else on the next function from today. When you check people in to a function on another day, the station asks you first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xIYWkhs6iS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Type part of a name, a nickname, a family name or a phone number. The results are grouped by family, so you check parents and children in together. People who have died are not listed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jMdgKhebFh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Tap the people who arrived (or Select all for a family) and click Check In. Press Enter to check in a single match at once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "MKovlKaxyJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Untick Print name tags to check people in without printing.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "oU0JPvXP15", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each person in the results shows their age, their grade and, in red, their allergies. A stethoscope icon means that the person has medical notes or an emergency contact: tap it to read them. Only Church Check-In, Church People Editor and Church Manager users see it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SMEcSRrOly", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Scan Card. A person can show their Member QR Card (see the People manual) or a pre check-in pass instead of saying their name. Click Scan Card and hold it in front of the camera. The camera works only when your site uses https.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1CAWeiqqYq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "New visitors", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Csg4n-FgzW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Click New Visitor, or Add them as a new visitor when a search finds no one. Confirm the name and the phone number, and click Add & Check In.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IPkU4WqiqY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The station first looks for people who are already in Churchit with the same name, or a similar name and the same phone number. If it finds someone, click Check In next to the right person: nobody new is added. Otherwise click Add as New Visitor.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SoHAjxIddc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The new person gets the Membership Visitor and the Source Check-In, so the member directory does not list them. They are checked in as a Guest.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gAkR3fUTGB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Type the Birth Date of a visiting child. For a child who comes without an adult in Churchit, open Emergency Contact and type a name and phone number.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Gl5OKlOEba", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Checked In list", "col": 12}}, {"id": "i6J8ldZOSj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The list on the right shows everyone checked in to the function, newest first, with their photo. It updates every 10 seconds, so you also see the check-ins of other stations. Type part of a name or a security code in Filter by name or code to find a person. The buttons on each row:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8dvM8Rh9Kq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Reprint the name tag.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kArA3uPBPC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Undo the check-in.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0As9Xn4tDo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Check out: for a person without a pickup tag, such as an adult or a volunteer, who left. A child with a pickup tag leaves only through Verify Pickup.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HknH0p5AdO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Page parents (the bell): sends a short message to each Adult of the child's household. An Adult who said yes to texts for Child Safety gets a text, and the others get an email. An Adult that a Pickup Restriction names for the child gets nothing. The station shows the names of the parents it reached. If it shows No parent reached, send a runner to find them. You can page the parents of one child once every 2 minutes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "arS8LQ2uJh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "After a person is checked out or collected, only the reprint button stays, and the check-in cannot be undone or deleted. Undoing or deleting a check-in removes the Checked-In row from the function's attendance.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2OCkCJnp-T", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Paging by text needs a gateway in SMS Settings with the Church Check-In role in its Allowed Roles. Otherwise the station sends emails only.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GgWnIAKeoW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Headcount", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9xL-XjfART", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Some people in a room do not check in by name. To count them, type the number of people in the room in the Headcount box under Checked In and click Save. The attendance total of the function is the larger of the headcount and the number of people counted by name. The box shows only once the function has started.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6L1Bi1yZD5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: The youth room has 23 teenagers, but only 15 checked in. The leader types 23 in Headcount. The function's attendance total is 23.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UqEmrxugRu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Team", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1sx-wnVoeV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Team tab lists the people who accepted a ministry team position at the function. Click Check In next to a name to check that person in as a Volunteer. Their name tag shows the word Volunteer and their position.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2QTVRvTMxF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Age and grade limits", "col": 12}}, {"id": "oLTEYDCEUu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In the Who Can Check In section on the Attendance tab of a Function, set Minimum Age, Maximum Age, Minimum Grade and Maximum Grade. The limits use the age and grade of the person on the day of the function. A person with no birth date (or no graduation year) does not pass an age (or grade) limit.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jhz0-CeJ3G", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "At the station, a person outside a limit shows a window with the reason: click Yes to check them in anyway, or No. The station checks a new visitor against the limits too. The kiosk and pre check-in do not offer the function to them. Volunteers have no limit check.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-fMUDCHstd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A recurring function gives its limits to each occurrence. You cannot check in to the template of a recurring function: the station shows only its dates.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_sBi9TSJr6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Room capacity", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CdOdAeWodJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The capacity of a function is the total Capacity of the rooms in its approved room bookings. With no approved booking, or rooms with no capacity, there is no limit. The people in the room are those who are checked in and not collected or checked out. Volunteers are not counted. Set Room Capacity in Check-In Settings:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vXNDUU4hJf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Off: no capacity check.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fL-BcYFjkC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Warn (at first): the check-in is saved, and the station shows an orange warning when the room is over capacity.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AroBsgP0xp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Block: the station, the kiosk, pre check-in and the Function Check-In form refuse a check-in when the room is full. A place opens again when a child is collected.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SBhrZoKHM2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Verify Pickup", "col": 12}}, {"id": "217g3cyyvN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use Verify Pickup when an adult comes to collect a child. It works only when Print Security Codes is ticked in Check-In Settings. A household keeps one code for the whole day, also for a child checked in later or at another function. No two households have the same code on one day.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8weQzNfpsb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Click Verify Pickup at the top of the Check-In Station.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gsvsAxfCHi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Type the 4 characters of the code on the adult's pickup tag and press Enter, or click Scan and hold the tag's QR code in front of the camera.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2sSFJz0Mru", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. The station shows each child checked in with this code today, with their photo and function. Below them, it shows who may collect them: the Adults of the household and the family's Authorized Pickups, with their photos. In red, it shows the Pickup Restrictions: who may not collect which child, and what to do.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "m-Qe-sAJHg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Compare the adult at the desk with these people. Release the child only to one of them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A5nyy9cwrT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. Keep a tick beside each child the adult is taking, and click Release beside the adult. Churchit records on each child's check-in who collected them, when, and which volunteer released them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "I7BIC_mHED", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Good to know", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dy9IMG0QbG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The station refuses to release a child to a restricted person. Only a Church Manager can override this, and must give a reason, which Churchit records with the manager's name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gQSKSyBKwq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- If the station shows No child is checked in with this code today, do not release the child. Ask a member of staff. A code from an earlier day does not work. If the station shows two families, ask for the child's name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RXuY5hUKYt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- In the Function Check-In list, pills show Awaiting Pickup, Picked Up and Checked Out. Add the Collected By and Collected At columns to see who collected each child and when.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Cr3Q54d-Z7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Authorized Pickups and Pickup Restrictions are kept on the Family (see the People manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZqFjoIlJVF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- With more than one church, the station finds only the check-ins of your church's functions and of shared functions.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QH6ZXXX84q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Name tags", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xQqyFp9qTC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A name tag prints for every check-in at the station. You can also print tags from a Function Check-In (Print Name Tag), from the Function Check-In list, or for any people from the Person list (Actions, then Print Name Tags).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lWvd68b1KA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In Check-In Settings:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NFEnivUC89", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Print Security Codes: for children's ministry. Everyone in one household gets the same code on their tag for the day, and an extra Pickup tag with their names and the code prints for the adult who collects them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rjYnuejshR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Print Allergies on Name Tags: prints a person's allergies, from the Allergies field of the Person, under their name. Pickup tags never show allergies.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "aMO_cHl8UM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Tag Formats by Kind: a different tag for Regular, Guest or Volunteer check-ins. New sites start with a Volunteer row that prints the word Volunteer and the position.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Iee-TSGaa5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Name tags print the person's Nickname, or their first name when they have none. Tags are print formats: Name Tag for the browser and Zebra Name Tag for Zebra printers. To change the layout, duplicate the format, edit the copy and choose it in Check-In Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ytY1VrSnFY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Label printer setup", "col": 12}}, {"id": "H-HvbuVkOK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Choose how tags reach the printer under Name Tag Printing in Check-In Settings, set the label size (4 × 2 in is the common Zebra name tag, 2.25 × 1.25 in the common Dymo one), and click Print Test Tag:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZhTlo76dXy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Browser: works with any printer that has a driver (Zebra, Dymo, Brother or an office printer). The print window opens for each batch. On a check-in computer, start Chrome with the --kiosk-printing option and make the label printer the default printer to skip the window.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eNzHMDsgpo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Zebra Browser Print: silent printing to a Zebra printer connected to the station computer. Install Zebra's free Browser Print app on that computer, make the printer its default, and allow this site when it asks. Set Printer DPI to match the printer (203 or 300).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IWmYHB-pWA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- QZ Tray: silent printing to any printer that the station computer can see. Install the free QZ Tray app and, if needed, type the Printer Name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CWhLCg4HDG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Network Printer: no software on the station computer. Type the IP address of a Zebra printer on the same network as the Churchit server. This needs a server on the church network.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0H6elAcJU5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With more than one church, add a row under Printers Per Church for each church that prints to its own printer. Fill in only what differs. A station always prints to the printer of its user's church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "K5BDQdhGpu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Self check-in kiosk", "col": 12}}, {"id": "snkIaR2IZb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A self check-in kiosk lets families check themselves in on a tablet or a computer at the door. It shows only today's functions whose Function Type has Allow Self Check-In ticked, from a time before the start (Self Check-In Opens (Minutes Before Start) in Check-In Settings, 60 at first) until the end.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Y1FqmuVUY8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To set up a kiosk:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ozBc21re5M", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Add a User for the kiosk device, with the role Church Check-In Kiosk and no other role. With more than one church, give it exactly one Church User Permission, for the church it serves. In Restrict IP, type the address of your church network, so that the login works only at church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r5W4-E9UV_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Tick Allow Self Check-In on each Function Type that families may check in to by themselves.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "U-40cicT7O", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. On the kiosk device, open /check-in-kiosk, sign in as the kiosk user and leave the page open.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jFXbi2F2BE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A family types its whole phone number: part of a number finds nobody. A person who is already checked in shows grey and cannot be ticked again. The kiosk shows the people of that household who may check in now, with their photo and grade.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JUApSXX_Yc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The family ticks who comes, picks a function when there is more than one, and taps Check In. The tags print through the printer settings of the kiosk's church. When the household already has a pickup code today, the kiosk prints the name tags without a new pickup tag: use the earlier one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mJ1IRWkuUp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The kiosk cannot add visitors, check people out or open any record. Children leave through Verify Pickup at the Check-In Station. QZ Tray does not work on the kiosk page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lIYIdINz38", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Pre check-in", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YTqI1hQINP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members can check in before they arrive. When a function of their church allows self check-in and check-in is open, a member opens Check-in in the member portal, ticks the people who come, picks the function and taps Show our pass. The pass holds a code. At the church, scan it: at the station with Scan Card, or at a kiosk with a handheld scanner. The people are checked in and their tags print.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qQcMIZ8Ivl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A member can choose only themselves and the children they may edit. To let an Adult also choose the other adults of the household, tick Adults may pre check in other adults in their household in Check-In Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iHp-sxVCjt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The code works only until the function ends, and only while check-in is open. A second scan checks in nobody new.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VV2Q84qnGW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🎵Songs", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hO6VJL9wis", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Songs list is your church's song library. Each song keeps its words as slides, its arrangements with chord charts, its rehearsal media and its copyright details. Add songs to the Schedule of a function to plan a service, show the words on a screen, and count the uses for your CCLI report.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fdOraQ4HH_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: The worship leader imports Amazing Grace from a SongSelect file. Churchit makes the song with its slides. She adds an arrangement in G with a ChordPro chart, and an MP3 for rehearsal. On Sunday's Function, she adds the song to the schedule in the key of A.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5mRP_dEFqB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The team sees the key A, the arrangement and the MP3 on the Serving page of the member portal, and the worship leader prints the chord chart in A from the desk. During the service, the song's slides show on the screen.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "I8hh4Uv73F", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add a song", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ANxbEBkCSl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Songs and click Add Song.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RI5cS1tDxB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Type the title, the CCLI number if you know it, and the Authors (the writers of the words and the music).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3iSpwWt3uL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. In the Copyright section, type the Copyright line as the publisher gives it. Tick Public Domain only when the words and the music are free of copyright.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "S7MZIE2Aen", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Fill in the Default Key (the key the team usually plays), the Tempo (BPM) and the Time Signature, such as 4/4.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DHBXj2Helt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. Add the words on the Slides tab, one slide for each verse or chorus.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "708GRAob8p", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "6. Save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1UkPWtezo4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add themes as tags in the sidebar of the form, such as Advent or Easter, then filter the Song list by tag. The Connections tab lists the functions whose schedule has the song.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NFN37ljnyX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Copyright on the screen. The last slide of a song shows its copyright and its CCLI number, with your church's CCLI License Number from the Church record. Visitors who are not signed in see the words of a song only when Public Domain is ticked.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wdGdkwmkey", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Present a song. Open the song and click Present to show its slides on a screen. To show a song inside a sermon presentation, add it as a slide to the sermon with no fields chosen (see the Study manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eIJNPaDAvn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Arrangements and chord charts", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5uklTmLOZ-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "An arrangement is one way that the team plays a song. Add arrangements on the Music tab, each with a name, a key, a tempo, notes and a ChordPro chart. Two arrangements of one song cannot have the same name. In a ChordPro chart, put each chord in square brackets before the syllable that you sing on it, for example [G]Amazing [D/F#]grace. Start each section with a line such as Verse 1 or Chorus, and leave a blank line between sections.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1HfPQxrL1i", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Chord Chart: save the song, click Chord Chart, and choose an arrangement and a key. The chart shows each chord above its words. When you choose another key, Churchit moves every chord to that key. A major key moves only to major keys, and a minor key only to minor keys. The arrangement or the song must have a key. Church Staff can open the chord chart.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "I4B2cF0k54", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Make Slides from ChordPro: click Actions, then Make Slides from ChordPro, and choose an arrangement. Churchit makes one slide for each section of the chart, with the words and no chords. This replaces all the slides of the song, so it asks you first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hrGrRHfOLJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Rehearsal media", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WxILcb3RWD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Add chord charts, lead sheets, audio and video in the Media table on the Music tab. Attach a file or type a link, and choose the arrangement it is for, or leave Arrangement empty for every arrangement. The people who serve at a function see the media of each song on its schedule on the Serving page of the member portal, until the function ends. They do not see it when they declined.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rplaghlUv4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Bring songs in", "col": 12}}, {"id": "J26wcNLuzh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Import Song Files: in the Song list, click Import Song Files and choose up to 50 ChordPro files (.cho, .chordpro, .chopro or .pro) or SongSelect files (.usr). Churchit makes one song for each file, with an arrangement named Default and one slide for each section. It skips a file when a song with the same CCLI number (or title) is already in your list. To get a .usr file, download the song from CCLI SongSelect. A .usr file has no chords.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nfjtLF4HEh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Add Public-Domain Hymns: in the Song list, click Add Public-Domain Hymns, choose from 33 hymns that are free of copyright, and click Add. Each one comes with Public Domain ticked, a chord chart and its slides. They come from WorshipCommons (worshipcommons.org), and you can change or delete them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-1rjS19Ldl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Export songs", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9UWGo-DPJF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To export one song, open it and click Actions, then Export. To export more, select them in the Song list and click Actions, then Export Songs. Choose OpenLyrics (words without chords, for FreeShow, OpenLP and Quelea) or ChordPro (the chart with chords). You can export up to 200 songs at a time, as a zip file. A song with no arrangement that has words is not exported.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FMoDAkrPmk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Song Usage and CCLI", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-KIDRKiqEL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Song Usage report counts how many times each song was on the Schedule of a function in a date range (the last six months at first), with its CCLI number and the date it was last used. It also counts in how many uses the words were displayed or printed, and in how many the function was streamed or recorded.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "r5nPM-HnBf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tick Displayed and Printed on the schedule row, and Streamed and Recorded on the function. CCLI has no public way to receive these numbers, so copy them into your CCLI report.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7B-_gXTqA1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Suggest Songs with AI", "col": 12}}, {"id": "t9lOTNyJ-X", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on (see the Foundations manual), save a Function, then click Actions, then Suggest Songs. The AI reads the title, Scripture and series of the sermon on the schedule, and the titles, tags, keys and last use of your songs. It never gets lyrics, charts or names of people. It suggests up to 8 of your own songs, each with a tick. Click Add to put the ticked songs on the schedule with their default key, then save the function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SQLaMfbcoh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🗂️Counseling Cases", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HAVqFs4Xu0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Counseling Case is a confidential file about pastoral counseling with one person: the person, the counselor, the case type, a summary, the status and a row for each meeting in the Sessions table. Only Church Pastoral Care and Church Manager users can open counseling cases.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "N9s04v0Esy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: A couple asks the pastor for marriage counseling. The pastor opens a Counseling Case for the husband with the type Marriage and the status Intake. After the first meeting, the status changes to Active and the pastor adds a session with a short note. After six sessions, the pastor sets the status to Closed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7So1h_jjZf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The status is Intake, Active, Closed or Referred (passed on to another counselor or service).
- You can add more Case Types in the Setup folder.
- With branch churches, only the person's own church can open a counseling case for them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AzNssQPifz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Counseling cases are kept more private than other records:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "C-cFb-XplC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A case never shows on the timeline of the Person form. It shows only on their Connections tab, to the people who may open it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2GA9pJJXQw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Churchit keeps no history of changes to a case. When you change or delete a session note, the old text is gone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PTRn0HK6Kc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A case is never sent to an AI model.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "C3r9_igRDu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When a person's data is removed, the case stays without its history and comments (see the People manual).", "col": 12}}]
